author_or_institution: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme
title: Report of the Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme
book_use: Chapter 4: Recommendation 17.1 calls for a consistent legal framework for automated government decisions, clear review paths, plain-language disclosure of automated decision-making, and access to business rules and algorithms for independent scrutiny; Recommendation 17.2 proposes monitoring and audit. Use as a safeguards case, not proof that all automation is abusive.

author_or_institution: Australian Government Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
title: Robodebt Royal Commission Implementation Update — March 2026
book_use: Chapter 4: Recommendation 17.1 is accepted but remains Ongoing as of March 2026; use to avoid implying Australia already has a completed universal automated-decision framework.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, consolidated 27 July 2026
book_use: Chapter 4: Article 86 provides a scoped right to clear and meaningful explanation for certain consequential decisions based on specified high-risk AI systems; Article 85 provides a complaint route. Article 113 reflects the 2026 implementation timetable. Do not generalize this into a universal right covering every AI-assisted decision.

title: Use of automated decision-making by government — Consultation paper
book_use: Chapter 4 counterevidence: automated decision-making is longstanding in Commonwealth administration; the department identified 46 primary statutes authorizing ADM with uneven safeguards. Supports a consistency-and-contestability argument rather than a ban on automation.
